story.name: ジャスミンの きっさてん
story.title: Too Many Drinks
story.line: メニューと なまえを きめます
story.ja: ジャスミンのメニューは22種類。キャラメルが試しに来るが、多すぎて選べない。マスターの「いちばん得意なものは？」で、5つにしぼる。店の名前は「リトル・ケトル」。きぬよが看板とカーテンを縫ってくれたが、看板のつづりが「LITLE」になっていた。きぬよは青くなるが、ジャスミンは笑いだし、そのままにすることにする。

segments.en: With the machine working, Pekoe sat down at the counter one night to write her menu. She was very excited. Maybe a little too excited.
By midnight, the menu had twenty-two drinks on it. There was a pumpkin spice latte, a lavender honey oat milk thing, and something called the Midnight Mocha Supreme.
The next morning, Goldie came by to be the very first taste tester. She sat down, opened the menu, and her smile slowly froze.
Wow. Okay. This is a lot of choices. Like, a lot. Can you give me a minute? Maybe ten minutes?
Ten minutes later, she was still reading. Fifteen minutes later, she closed the menu, looked up, and asked very politely for a glass of water.
I'm sorry, I just couldn't decide. Everything sounds good, but I kind of panicked halfway down the page.
Pekoe made her a little of everything anyway. Goldie tried them all, bravely. By the end, she was talking very fast and her ears were twitching.
Okay, that one's amazing. That one's also amazing. I think I can hear colors now. Is that normal? That can't be normal.
That afternoon, Pekoe took the menu up to The Roost. Brewster read the whole thing from top to bottom without changing his face at all.
Too many. What do you make best? Not what's interesting. What do you make best, when you're tired, on a Tuesday?
Pekoe thought about it on the walk home. She thought about the mornings on her porch, and what her friends always asked for again.
In the end, she crossed out almost everything. The new menu fit on one small card.
Drip coffee. A latte. A pot of black tea. Hot cocoa. And honey toast.
Five things. That's it. And I'm going to make every one of them really, really well.
Then there was the question of a name. She wrote ideas on the back of receipts for days.
The Pier Café. Bean There. Pekoe's Place. None of them felt right.
And then one evening, the old kettle on her stove started to whistle, the same kettle she had used since she first moved to the island.
The Little Kettle. Oh, that's it. That's the one. That's exactly what it's supposed to feel like.
Mabel heard about the name and offered to make a sign. She also offered to make curtains, cushions, and matching aprons, because Mabel can't help herself.
Oh, honey, leave it to me. I'll stitch the sign myself. It'll be ready by Friday, I promise.
On Friday, Mabel arrived with a big package wrapped in brown paper. The curtains were yellow with tiny white flowers. The aprons matched. Everything was perfect.
Then they unrolled the sign. It was beautiful, stitched in blue thread on soft cream fabric.
And it said, in big, proud letters, The Litle Kettle. Little, with only one T.
Oh no. Oh, no, no, no. I was up so late finishing it. I'm so sorry, sweetie. I can take it all out and start over.
Pekoe looked at the sign for a long moment. And then she started to laugh. And then Mabel started to laugh, and they couldn't stop.
Don't you dare change it. I love it. It's a little kettle. It doesn't need two T's. It's little.
So they hung it over the door, just like that. And people would ask about it for years, and Pekoe would always tell them it was on purpose.
That night, the café was ready. The menu was short, the curtains were up, and the sign was spelled wrong. Opening day was on Sunday.
Pekoe checked the weather forecast on her phone before bed. She looked at it once, then twice, and then she decided not to look at it again.

predict.ask: 日曜の オープンの 日は どうなる？
choices: It's sunny, and a long line forms before she opens.
It pours rain, and at first nobody comes.
The sign falls down and lands in the sea.
predict.ja: 大雨で、はじめはだれも来ない。
